summary.text: The Space Shuttle was a retired, partially reusable NASA spacecraft system that flew to low Earth orbit from 1981 to 2011.
Five orbiters flew 135 missions that launched satellites, probes and the Hubble Space Telescope, and helped build and service the International Space Station.
It launched upright like a conventional rocket with two boosters and an external tank, and the orbiter glided back to a runway landing.

facts.label: Main engines
facts.value: Three Rocketdyne RS-25 engines on the orbiter

items.prompt: How did a shuttle orbiter survive coming back through the atmosphere and reach the ground?

options.label: A heat shield fell away and parachutes lowered it into the ocean
Its main engines fired all the way down for an upright landing
Protective tiles shielded it, then it glided to a runway landing
It folded its wings and was caught by a carrier aircraft

items.explain: The orbiter was protected during reentry by its thermal protection system tiles and glided as a spaceplane to a runway landing.

items.prompt: After a shuttle launch, which major part of the stack was not recovered for reuse?

options.label: The pair of solid rocket boosters
The tank holding liquid hydrogen and liquid oxygen
The orbiter itself
The three main engines

items.explain: The solid rocket boosters were recoverable and the orbiter flew home, while the external tank was expendable.

items.prompt: An orbiter landed in California instead of Florida. How did it get back to Kennedy Space Center?

options.label: Carried on top of a specially modified Boeing 747
Flown back under its own engine power
Floated home on a barge across the Gulf
Rolled across the country on a giant trailer

items.explain: If the landing occurred at Edwards, the orbiter was flown back to the Kennedy Space Center atop the Shuttle Carrier Aircraft, a modified Boeing 747.

items.prompt: Why did the first orbiter, Enterprise, never reach orbit?

options.label: It was lost in an accident before its first launch
Its heat tiles failed every test
It was only a display model made of wood
It had no orbital capability and was used for landing tests

items.explain: Enterprise was built in 1976 and used in Approach and Landing Tests, but had no orbital capability.

items.prompt: Max Faget patented a fully recoverable design with straight wings. What objection did the Air Force raise?

options.label: Straight wings would make the booster too heavy to leave the pad
Straight wings could not stand the heat and stress of reentry or give enough sideways reach
The design needed too many engines to be built
The design could not carry any crew

items.explain: The Air Force Flight Dynamics Laboratory argued a straight-wing design could not withstand the thermal and aerodynamic stresses of reentry and would not give the required cross-range capability.

items.prompt: After the Shuttle retired in 2011, how did the US send astronauts to the ISS until May 2020?

options.label: It rented seats on Chinese spacecraft
It kept a single orbiter in reserve
It relied on Russian Soyuz spacecraft
It sent no astronauts at all

items.explain: The US relied on the Russian Soyuz spacecraft from the last Shuttle flight until the launch of the Crew Dragon Demo-2 mission in May 2020.
